title: Wait for a condition
summary: An explicit wait checks for a condition until a time limit. It is more useful than always sleeping a fixed length.
introduction: An explicit wait checks for a condition until a time limit. It is more useful than always sleeping a fixed length. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: An explicit wait checks for a condition until a time limit. It is more useful than always sleeping a fixed length.

blocks.code:
from urllib.parse import quote from selenium import webdriver from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By driver = webdriver.Chrome() try: driver.get("data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + quote('

Ready

')) from selenium.webdriver.support.ui import WebDriverWait from selenium.webdriver.support import expected_conditions as EC item = WebDriverWait(driver, 5).until(EC.visibility_of_element_located((By.ID, "ready"))) assert item.text == "Ready" finally: driver.quit()
blocks.title: Wait for a condition

blocks.text: The wait returns when the Ready element is visible, or fails after its limit.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not use long fixed sleeps to hide a timing problem.
